reason: While the passage includes ritual and ceremonial instructions (קִדַּשְׁתָּם - sanctification, כִבְּסוּ שִׂמְלֹתָם - washing garments), these are presented as preparatory measures rather than as intrinsically important to Yahweh. The text's primary emphasis is on the holiness and sanctity of Yahweh's presence (יְרֵד יְהוָה), the establishment of boundaries to protect people from divine danger (הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם עֲלוֹת בָּהָר), and warnings about approaching the mountain (כָּל־ הַנֹּגֵעַ בָּהָר מוֹת יוּמָֽת). The rituals function as instrumental means to prepare the people for safe encounter with Yahweh's holiness, not as ends in themselves that are valued by Yahweh.
